in_hebrew.name: קמל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם קמל נגזר מהמילה 'קאמל' הערבית, המתייחסת לחיית הבדואים והמדבר. בברית החדשה, הקאמל אינו מופיע כשם. עם זאת, חיית המדבר הופיעה בקדושתה בברית הישנה (קטורג, 3:7; 11:24). השם קמל יכול לרמז לחיים של הדרך, סבלנות, ויכולת לשרוד בסביבות קשות. בתרבות הנוצרית, חיית המדבר סמלה לבני-אדם שהם יכולים לשרוד בסביבות קשות וללכת בדרך האמונה בגלל סבלנותם ויכולתם להעמיד פנים.

in_greek.name: Κάμηλος
in_greek.meaning: ζώον των βεδουίνων, ζώον του έρματος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κάμηλος προέρχεται από την αραβική λέξη κάμιλ, η οποία αναφέρεται στο ζώο των Βεδουίνων και του έρματος. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το Κάμηλος δεν εμφανίζεται ως όνομα. Ωστόσο, το ζώο του έρματος εμφανίζεται στην Παλαιά Διαθήκη (Κτησιάσκων, 3,7 και 11,24). Το όνομα Κάμηλος μπορεί να αναφέρεται στη ζωή της路ς, στη σωστότητα και στη δυνατότητα να επιβιώσει σε δύσκολες συνθήκες. Στη χριστιανική κουλτούρα, το ζώο του έρματος συμβολίζει τους ανθρώπους που μπορούν να επιβιώσουν σε δύσκολες συνθήκες και να περάσουν από την πίστη λόγω ησυχίας και δυνατότητας να αντιμετωπίζουν τις δοκιμασίες.

in_latin.name: Camelus
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Camellus a vocabulo Arabico Camelum derivatur, quod referatur ad animal Beduinorum et deserti. In Novo Testamento, Camelus non apparit. Sed animal deserti apparuit in Veteri Testamento (Ctesias, 3,7 et 11,24). Nomen Camellus potest significare vitam viae, constantiam, et facultatem supervivendi in difficilibus circumstantiis. In cultura Christiana, animal deserti symbolizat homines qui possunt supervivere in difficilibus circumstantiis et percurrere per fidem propter constantiam et facultatem superariendo difficultates.

in_english.name: Camel
in_english.meaning: a desert animal, specifically one that lives in the deserts of the Middle East
in_english.long_meaning: The name Camel is derived from the Arabic word كَمَل (kamal), which refers to a desert animal and the dromedary. In the New Testament, the Camel does not appear as a name. However, the desert animal appears in the Old Testament (Ctesias, 3:7 and 11:24). The name Camel can symbolize a life of the road, constancy, and the ability to survive in harsh conditions. In Christian culture, the desert animal symbolizes men who can survive in harsh conditions and walk by faith due to their constancy and ability to overcome difficulties.

data.cultural_impact: Camels have been an integral part of Middle Eastern history and culture, particularly for their ability to traverse vast desert landscapes. Given the harsh conditions of these environments, the use of camels enabled the expansion of trade and commerce between civilizations. In addition, they played a vital role in religious, military, and cultural practices, particularly in the Middle East and North Africa.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, camels are used as symbols of strength, endurance, and the journey of life. The Old Testament book of Psalms mentions camels in the context of God's provision and guidance. In the New Testament, Jesus uses the parable of the camel passing through the eye of a needle to illustrate the difficulty of entering the Kingdom of Heaven (Matthew 19:23-24). Through this symbolism, camels serve as reminders of God's strength, guidance, and the necessity of embracing the challenges of life with faith and perseverance.

historical_references.reference: Camelus dromedarius, the one-humped camel, is native to the Arabian Peninsula and was domesticated around 3000 BC.
historical_references.context: Camels were used for transportation and food in ancient civilizations.
